findings.description: Generic subprocess wrapper run_cmd(cmd) flagged as command execution; cmd is a caller-supplied argv list with no shell=True
findings.code_snippet:
def run_cmd(cmd):
    process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, universal_newlines=True, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="utf-8")
findings.reasoning: Popen is called without shell=True, so cmd is executed directly as argv. The wrapper itself is not an injection sink; exploitability depends on whether callers pass untrusted strings as argv elements. Callers are internal (interpreter discovery and tooling), so there is no remote attacker-controlled input path.

findings.description: Periodic update spawns a background Python process whose inline code is built with str.format using {!r} escaping
findings.reasoning: cmd is [sys.executable, "-c", code] with no shell. The inline code embeds distribution, paths, and search dirs via {!r}, which yields valid Python literals, so values are not interpreted as code beyond literal escaping. Inputs are local configuration, so this is low risk. Flagging as fp with a note that repr-based embedding is the safe pattern here.
